ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: There are two mutually overlapping dashed circular rings in the image. The upper circular ring contains the numbers 9, X, 8, 11, Y, 9 in order; the lower circular ring contains Y, 11, 14, 2, 13, 7. The problem requires that the sum of the numbers in each circular ring is 55. First look at the lower circular ring: Y + 11 + 14 + 2 + 13 + 7 = 55. The sum of the known numbers is 11 + 14 + 2 + 13 + 7 = 47, so Y = 55 - 47 = 8. Then look at the upper circular ring: 9 + X + 8 + 11 + Y + 9 = 55. Substituting Y = 8 gives 9 + X + 8 + 11 + 8 + 9 = 55, the sum of the known numbers is 45, so X = 55 - 45 = 10.

method.method_draft: Read the two rings in the image and note that the upper and lower rings share the same two circles, Y and 11. Since the text says both ring sums are 55, the non-shared parts of the two rings must have equal sums after canceling the shared Y and 11. The upper non-shared numbers are 9, 9, X, and 8; the lower non-shared numbers are 7, 13, 2, and 14. Set 9 + 9 + X + 8 = 7 + 13 + 2 + 14. Thus X + 26 = 36, so X = 10.
